Certified type: Multi-Dimensional Measuring instrument, Type: JORO Volume
Category — "Multi-Dimensional Measuring instrument" — this is for R129 (Multi-dimensional measuring instruments — measuring the volume of stacks of round timber or bulk material). Category could be "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument".

Scheme: A
Recommendation: R129, edition 2000 (year edition — schema says edition int, so 2000).

Test reports: No. NMi-1902248-01 dated 13 December 2021, 59 pages, role: type_evaluation_report.

Characteristics table:
- Principle of operation: reflection of light
- Maximum dimension: Length max ≤ 2500 cm; Width max ≤ 300 cm; Height max ≤ 450 cm
- Minimum dimension: min ≥ 100 cm for all three (Length, Width, Height)
- Scale interval d: d ≥ 5 cm (for all three)
- Measuring range: Single interval
- Speed range: 0 km/h ≤ v ≤ 5 km/h
- Electromagnetic environment class: E2
- Mechanical environment class: M2
- Component-specific: measuring sensors vs controller PC:
  - temperature range: -25 °C / +40 °C (sensors), -10 °C / +40 °C (PC)
  - humidity: condensing (sensors), non-condensing (PC)
  - intended location: open and closed (sensors), closed (PC)
- Power supply voltage: 24 V DC
- Method of operation: automatic
- Application: round timber stacked on truck etc., bulk material in tipper
- Limitations of use: Round timber and opaque bulk material
- Software identification version number: 1.1.x.x (x is non-relevant, 0-99)

Components: The measuring sensors and The controller PC are components. Record components with roles.

Characteristics:
- type_level:
  - principle_of_operation: "reflection of light"
  - speed_range: value {min: 0, max: 5}, unit "km/h"
  - electromagnetic_environment_class: "E2"
  - mechanical_environment_class: "M2"
  - measuring_range: "Single interval"
  - power_supply_voltage: 24, unit "V", and power_supply_type "DC"
  - method_of_operation: "automatic"
  - software_version_number: "1.1.x.x" — this is a pattern, keep as string.

For dimensions per axis (length/width/height), these vary by axis — configuration axis? It's attribute × axis (length, width, height). Use config_level with axis "dimension":

- maximum_length: {min: null, max: 2500}, unit cm
- maximum_width: {min: null, max: 300}, unit cm
- maximum_height: {min: null, max: 450}, unit cm
- minimum_length/width/height: {min: 100, max: null}, unit cm
- scale_interval: {min: 5, max: null}, unit cm (same for all three; could be type_level)

Actually schema config_level: {attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}}. I could do config_level entries:

attribute: "maximum_dimension", axis: "dimension", values: [{condition: "length", value: {min:null, max:2500}, unit_symbol:"cm"}, ...]

Or just use distinct attributes. Simpler: use config_level with attribute "maximum_dimension" axis "dimension". Or flatten to maximum_length etc. I think config_level is appropriate here. Alternatively, type_level with attributes maximum_length, maximum_width, maximum_height. Hmm. The schema says config_level is for "attribute × config-axis matrix". Dimensions × axis is such a matrix. I'll use config_level.

Components config-level characteristics: temperature range, humidity, intended location vary by component (measuring sensors vs controller PC). Use config_level with axis "component":

- temperature_range, axis "component", values: [{condition: "measuring sensors", value: {min:-25, max:40}, unit_symbol:"°C"}, {condition: "controller PC", value: {min:-10, max:40}, unit_symbol:"°C"}]
- humidity: [{condition: "measuring sensors", value: "condensing"}, {condition: "controller PC", value: "non-condensing"}]
- intended_location: [{condition: "measuring sensors", value: "open and closed"}, {condition: "controller PC", value: "closed"}]

Components:
- {role: "Measuring sensors", type_designations: [], ...} — no type designation given. Maybe just record role and characteristics inline? The schema says components[] with role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. But characteristics isn't defined in the components entry in the schema... Actually it says "components[]: role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}". So I can include sub-characteristics per component. Let me put temperature range etc. there.

Actually let me be careful: schema yaml lists:
```
components[]:                       # include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies
  role, type_designations[], alternatives ("OR"|"AND"|null), characteristics{}
```
So components have characteristics{} too. But then rule 5 says use characteristics.config_level for config axes. Either is acceptable. I'll use components with their own characteristics and maybe also skip config_level to avoid duplication. Hmm, but the example R60 shows characteristics at top-level type_level etc. For safety, I'll include the component-level characteristics within components[] entries, and not duplicate in config_level. Actually maybe include both? Duplication risk. I'll put them in components[] characteristics — that seems most faithful.

Wait, but rules 5 says "When attributes vary by configuration ... use characteristics.config_level". Component is a configuration axis. Hmm. But the components entry with characteristics{} is designed for sub-assemblies. I'll do components with characteristics, and also add config_level entries for temperature/humidity/location keyed by component? That could be redundant but the schema allows it. I think I'll put component characteristics in components[] only, to keep it clean. Actually, let me follow rule 5 more strictly: the temperature range differs by component, which is config-axis. But components[] exists precisely to hold sub-assembly characteristics. The schema comment "characteristics{}" in components implies sub-characteristics go there. I'll do that.

Scale interval d ≥ 5 cm: same for all dimensions — type_level: scale_interval_d: {min: 5, max: null}, unit "cm".

Maximum dimension per axis via config_level:
```
{
  "attribute": "maximum_dimension",
  "axis": "dimension",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "length", "value": {"min": null, "max": 2500}, "unit_symbol": "cm", "unit_id": null},
    {"condition": "width", "value": {"min": null, "max": 300}, "unit_symbol": "cm"},
    {"condition": "height", "value": {"min": null, "max": 450}, "unit_symbol": "cm"}
  ]
}
```
Note: schema for config_level values says {condition, value} — but rule 5 says values follow same structured form {condition, value, unit_symbol}. OK.

Similarly minimum_dimension with all three {min: 100, max: null}.

Scale interval: could also be config_level with all three 5. But type_level single entry is fine since it's the same.

model_family: only one type, no variants — omit (schema says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant).

matrix_tables: none needed.

recommendation: id "R129", edition 2000, scheme "A".

Accuracy classes: not mentioned — omit.
